title: Onboarding checklist and rollout constraints for community-trained model variants
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Clarify and formalize the Product Requirements for admitting community-trained open models into the Redwood model catalog when teams request unpinned or alias variants. This PRD defines the minimum intake checklist, compatibility probes, safe-rollout constraints, and required telemetry/rollback signals. It captures scope changes from the previous lightweight intake draft to include provenance/licensing checks, quantization validation, and explicit KV-cache / prefix-caching compatibility notes.
scope_changes: Expanded from a minimal metadata-only intake to a two-stage admission flow: (1) metadata + provenance + quick runtime probe; (2) staged canary with evals and telemetry gating. Added mandatory license/weights provenance documentation and a lightweight quantization sanity test. These changes increase cross-team dependencies (Security, Serving, Research).
acceptance_criteria: A single-page onboarding checklist exists and is stored in Confluence (link below) and covers metadata, provenance, license, intended use, and security flags.

Runtime compatibility probe: automated smoke test that runs generate/embedding paths on representative sequence lengths and returns pass/fail and perf metrics (p90 latency under configured threshold for that model class).

Quantization validation: guidance and a test harness run that checks model outputs against FP32 baseline on a set of 50 curated prompts with a tolerance threshold; failures must be triaged and documented.
Pin semantics documented: clear definitions for hard-pin, soft-pin, and alias variants with examples and fallback behaviors; runtime must accept pin metadata and enforce fallbacks at request time.

Staged rollout plan: canary traffic gating with automatic rollback triggers defined (error spike > 2x baseline, quality regression measured by eval set > defined threshold, or p99 latency increase > 30%).
Telemetry: model-level tracing, per-variant token breakdown, and two new metrics instrumented (compatibility_probe_pass, quant_diff_score) and visible in console dashboards for 30 days during canary.
Security & legal: license verification sign-off by Security/Legal and provenance artifacts attached to catalog entry before public routing is allowed.
Playbook: documented runbook for incidents related to newly admitted community models including rollback steps and notification list.
rollout_plan: Stage 0 - Intake: PM fills checklist and attaches provenance + license docs; Security does quick scan (48h).
Stage 1 - Probe: Infra runs automated compatibility probe on dedicated dev infra; result recorded as pass/fail.
Stage 2 - Canary: Deploy variant to dedicated canary pool (5-10% traffic) with enhanced tracing and 30-day retention.
Stage 3 - Expand: Conditional ramp to 50% then 100% after 2 successful weekly evaluations with no regression.
Stage 4 - Monitor & Iterate: Keep enhanced telemetry for 30 days post full rollout; schedule a postmortem for any significant deviation.
additional_requirements: Catalog UI must display pin type and a short compatibility summary on the model page.
API must accept variant alias metadata and return active fallback variant when requested variant is unavailable.
Serving runtime must expose a lightweight probe endpoint that returns kernel/quantization compatibility hints.
Evals team to provide a 50-prompt baseline set for regression checks; Research to maintain threshold guidance per model family.
outstanding_questions: What is the minimum acceptable provenance artifact for community weights (SHA256 + origin URL vs signed attestation)?
Do we allow models with permissive but incompatible licenses for some enterprise customers (surface as 'restricted' flag)?
What is the rollback latency SLA expectations across Dedicated vs Hosted routes when a canary triggers a rollback?
